notes: Re-extracted 17 October 2026 from the guide and evidence as updated on main (807973d) for the a116616 build. The earlier extraction's five contradictions with the installed build (close default, placeholder copy, buttonSlot, region role, testID) are resolved in the guide, and the guide now says Nudge sets the Nudge&Alert context itself, confirmed in the evidence. The 'always set all three' sentence is gone, so nothing in this entry is ambiguous any more. The removal-announcement gap still rests on the 7 October check. The guide names no other component to use instead, so avoidWhen is empty. The examples pass only Color Mode and appearance: the Nudge sets its own Context. Re-extracted 29 October 2026 (Penny run run_19b90d38) for the c8526ae publish (#206): the close label is no longer fixed (closeAccessibilityLabel) and stacked-detailed now warns about ignored props, so those two gaps are removed; the Sources quote on the close label is replaced. Refreshed 29 October 2026 for guide fix #543 (3f56271): the Anatomy note for the button now names it a small Button; /anatomy/3 quotes the new sentence.

useWhen.text: A short suggestion with one action, such as splitting a payment, that sits within a screen's content.

from.quote: Use a Nudge for a short suggestion with one action, such as splitting a payment, that sits within a screen’s content.

anatomy.holds: The startSlot: a 20 px sparkle by default; it can be swapped or removed.

from.quote: A 20 px sparkle by default; it can be swapped or removed.

anatomy.holds: title, 14 px bold; says what's on offer in a line.

anatomy.holds: body, 12 px; one sentence of detail.

anatomy.holds: The one next step, as a small Button (buttonLabel and onPressButton, or buttonSlot).

from.quote: Tinted by its appearance mode, with 12 px padding.

configuration.text: Choose the type for the space and content you have, and an appearance mode for its colour.

from.quote: Choose the type for the space and content you have, and an appearance mode for its colour.

configuration.text: stacked-prominent, the default: a title and body stacked beside the icon, the button below.

from.quote: The default: a title and body stacked beside the icon, the button below.

configuration.text: inline-compact: one line of text with the button beside it; it has no title.

from.quote: One line of text with the button beside it. It has no title.

configuration.text: stacked-detailed: a title over your own content, such as list items; no button or close.

from.quote: A title over your own content, such as list items. No button or close.

configuration.text: Use stacked-detailed for a list: a title over list items explains the offer.

from.quote: A title over list items explains the offer.

configuration.text: Do not expect an action on stacked-detailed: it ignores the button and close, so people have nothing to tap.

from.quote: It ignores the button and close, so people have nothing to tap.

configuration.text: Show the close button when people may dismiss the nudge.

from.quote: Add a close button when people may dismiss it

configuration.text: On stacked-prominent and inline-compact, the close button shows only when onClose is set or showClose is true; showClose false hides it even with onClose, and stacked-detailed never renders it.
The default button renders when buttonLabel or onPressButton is set; buttonSlot set to null removes it.
Leave Context to the Nudge: it sets the Nudge&Alert context itself, so its button is Figma's small size.

from.quote: Nudge sets the Nudge&Alert context itself, so its button is Figma’s small size.

configuration.text: Do not pass another Context on the Nudge or through a container around it: a Default Context makes the button 42 px, and it outweighs the message.

from.quote: A Default Context, set here or passed down by a container, makes the button 42 px; it outweighs the message.

configuration.text: Remove the sparkle when the message needs no accent: set startSlot to null.

from.quote: Remove the sparkle when the message needs no accent.

configuration.text: AppearanceBrand tints the card, body, icon and button together.

from.quote: AppearanceBrand tints the card, body, icon, and button together.

configuration.text: Figma's white card with a purple icon matches no single appearance mode; Neutral is the closest.

from.quote: Figma’s white card with a purple icon matches no single appearance mode; Neutral is the closest.

states.when: The card isn't interactive; its button and close button have their own pressed and focus states.

from.quote: The card isn’t interactive. Its button and close button have their own pressed and focus states.

states.when: Pressing the X calls onClose and the screen hides the nudge: Nudge has no hidden state of its own.

from.quote: Nudge has no hidden state: after a close, the screen removes it.

accessibility.text: Give a stacked card a title: on the web a card with a title is a region named by its title (inline-compact shows no title).

from.quote: On the web a card with a title is a region named by its title

accessibility.text: Set onPressButton for the button and onClose for the close button: Enter and Space activate them only when those are set, and without them the button is focusable but does nothing.

from.quote: Enter and Space activate them only when `onPressButton` / `onClose` are set; without them the button is focusable but does nothing.

absolute.reason: "only" states when the default button and close respond; it does not apply to a buttonSlot or closeSlot, which bring their own handlers.

accessibility.text: The close button's label for screen readers can be changed with closeAccessibilityLabel.

from.quote: its label for screen readers can be changed.

examples.purpose: A split-payment suggestion on a payment screen, in a lavender appearance; the screen handles the button and removes the nudge on close.
examples.jsx:
<Nudge
  title="Split payment"
  body="Pay ₹12,000 in 3 monthly instalments."
  buttonLabel="See plans"
  onPressButton={() => {}}
  onClose={() => {}}
  modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', AppearanceBrand: 'Secondary' }}
/>

from.quote: The screen handles its button and removes it on close.

examples.purpose: Inline compact, with no close button: one line of text with the button beside it.
examples.jsx:
<Nudge
  type="inline-compact"
  body="Set up autopay so you never miss a bill."
  buttonLabel="Set up"
  onPressButton={() => {}}
  showClose={false}
  modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}
/>

from.quote: One line of text with the button beside it. It has no title.

examples.purpose: Stacked detailed: a title over list items, with no button or close.
examples.jsx:
<Nudge type="stacked-detailed" title="Why split this payment?" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="No extra cost" supportText="You pay ₹12,000 in total" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
  <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Three monthly payments" supportText="₹4,000 on the 5th of each month" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
</Nudge>

from.quote: A title over list items explains the offer.

evidenceFacts.name: title
evidenceFacts.description: On the web, with a title the card is a region named by the title; without one it has no role.
evidenceFacts.quote: with a `title`, the card is a `<section role="region">` named by the title

evidenceFacts.name: onClose
evidenceFacts.description: Only reports the press; the screen removes the nudge.
evidenceFacts.quote: `onClose` only reports the press; the consumer removes the nudge.

evidenceFacts.name: closeSlot
evidenceFacts.description: Replaces the default close, an IconButton ic_close labelled “Close” with forced Neutral / Low / S modes.
evidenceFacts.quote: The close button is always `IconButton ic_close`, labelled "Close", with forced Neutral / Low / S modes.

evidenceFacts.name: children
evidenceFacts.description: Replaces the title, body and button in stacked-prominent; the body and button in inline-compact; the list in stacked-detailed.
evidenceFacts.quote: `children` (replaces title, body, and button in prominent; body and button in compact; the list in detailed)

evidenceFacts.name: modes
evidenceFacts.description: Slot children get the Nudge's modes.
evidenceFacts.quote: Slot children get the Nudge's modes.

evidenceFacts.name: Context
evidenceFacts.description: When the merged modes have no Context, Nudge sets Nudge&Alert itself (Figma's small button). A Default Context, on the Nudge or on a container whose modes reach it, gives a 42 px button.
evidenceFacts.quote: when the merged modes have no `Context`, Nudge sets `Context: 'Nudge&Alert'` itself

evidenceFacts.name: showClose
evidenceFacts.description: Since a116616 (the #271 fix), Close renders only when onClose is set or showClose is true, and showClose false hides it even with onClose.
evidenceFacts.quote: Close renders only when `onClose` is set or `showClose` is true, and `showClose={false}` hides it even with `onClose`.

evidenceFacts.name: buttonSlot
evidenceFacts.description: null or false removes the button, leaving the title and body.

gaps.text: In Color Mode Dark the title stays #1e1a14 on a dark card (#208): the title colour is one literal for every mode.
gaps.quote: `nudge/title/color` is still one literal #1e1a14 for every mode (#208)

gaps.text: No appearance mode reproduces Figma's white card with a purple icon.
gaps.quote: no mode for Figma's white card with a purple icon

gaps.text: inline-compact never shows the title, but still uses it as the region's name, an invisible name.
gaps.quote: inline-compact never shows `title` but still uses it as the region's name (an invisible name)

gaps.text: onPressButton without buttonLabel renders an empty, unnamed button.
gaps.quote: `onPressButton` without `buttonLabel` renders an empty, unnamed button

gaps.text: The sparkle icon isn't hidden from assistive tech on the web.
gaps.quote: the sparkle SVG isn't hidden from assistive tech on the web

gaps.text: Nothing is announced and focus is not managed when a nudge is removed.
gaps.quote: No announcement or focus management when a nudge is removed.
